Each customer comes with a variety of deployment needs, cost optimization and security.  You would own the machinery that makes this repeatable. The job is to take a stack with many moving parts, including agent runtimes, policy and redaction layers, evaluation pipelines, and vector stores, and make it install cleanly in places we don't control. You would also keep it running once it's there. We are a small, fast team, so you will have real influence over how we build, and you will ship things in your first month. What you'll do Design and run the pipelines, infrastructure code, and release process that take Pravar AI from commit to customer environment. Write Terraform and Helm packaging that behaves the same way on AWS, Azure, GCP, and bare-metal Kubernetes. Build deployment paths that hold up under customer change-control and approval gates. Treat the air-gapped install as a design constraint from the start, not a special case added later. Manage observability and reliability across those environments: metrics, logs, traces, alerting, and runbooks. Own the SLOs we commit to, and lead the incident reviews that follow when we miss one. Own backup, failover, and disaster recovery, and test them on a schedule rather than trusting the diagram. Build vulnerability scanning, dependency checks, and image validation into the pipeline. Manage secrets and certificates, and support customer-managed encryption keys. Help collect the evidence our SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 42001 work requires, and make that collection routine. Build the tooling behind our delegated support model: just-in-time access, session recording, and least-privilege roles. Work at the cutting edge of product availability and enterprise requirements, with room to try new things. What we're looking for Four to six years in DevOps, platform engineering, or SRE, with at least two years running production systems that other people depended on. Real experience deploying in both worlds. You have shipped to public cloud and to customer-controlled or on-premises infrastructure, and you know how different the two feel when something breaks at 2 a.m. Strong Kubernetes and Helm skills , including ingress, autoscaling, network policy, and upgrades without downtime. Infrastructure as code in practice. Terraform or something equivalent, written for reuse and not just for a single environment. CI/CD fluency in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or ArgoCD, along with sound release habits: versioning, promotion, rollback. Working knowledge of observability (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenSearch, or comparable) and a feel for what is worth alerting on. Solid Linux, networking, and scripting. You can debug DNS, TLS, and IAM problems without a long detour, and you write Bash or Python when a task calls for it. A security-minded habit of mind. Least privilege, secrets handling, and encryption in transit and at rest are things you do by default. Comfort with ambiguity and pace. review_candidates.description: Job Description If you’ve ever considered a job in IT, become an Information Technology Specialist in the Army National Guard and expand your skills and experience with complex technologies. In this role, you will be responsible for sending, receiving, and processing messages and data on the Guard’s sophisticated networks. You will also maintain and troubleshoot the systems that support the military’s logistics and classified data, and build firewalls that can withstand any attempted cyberattack. Job Duties Maintenance of networks, hardware, and software Provide customer and network administration services Construct, edit, and test computer programs Some Of The Skills You’ll Learn Use of computer consoles and peripheral equipment Computer systems concepts Planning, designing, and testing computer systems Helpful Skills Interest in computer science Strong attention to detail Ability to communicate effectively Experience in installation of computers Through your training, you will develop the skills and experience to enjoy a civilian career working as a network support technician, data processing technician, or computer programmer in just about any company that uses computers. Earn While You Learn Instead of paying to learn these skills, get paid to learn. In the Army National Guard, you will learn these valuable job skills while earning a regular paycheck and qualifying for tuition assistance. Job training for an Information Technology Specialist consists of 10 weeks of Basic Training, where you'll learn basic Soldiering skills, and 20 weeks of Advanced Individual Training (AIT) with classroom instruction. Benefits/Requirements Benefits Paid training A monthly paycheck Montgomery GI Bill Federal and State tuition assistance Retirement benefits for part-time service Low-cost life insurance (up to $400,000 in coverage) 401(k)-type savings plan Student Loan Repayment Program (up to $50,000, for existing loans) Health care benefits available VA home loans Bonuses, if applicable Most non-prior service candidates will earn between $200 and $250 per drill weekend, subject to change Requirements Military enlistment in the Army National Guard Must be at least a junior in high school, or have a high school diploma or a GED certificate Must be between the ages of 17 and 35 Must be able to pass a physical exam and meet legal and moral standards Must meet citizenship requirements (see NATIONALGUARD.com for details) Requires military enlistment. Programs and benefits are subject to change. Ask your Army National Guard recruiter for the most up-to-date information. Actual MOS assignment may depend on MOS availability. Email me jobs like this
